title: Signal smoothing notes for pool-level drift and cluster rollups
content:
Context and purpose:

Quick working notes for the dashboard export we pulled 2026-03-24 -> 2026-03-28 (daily samples) across clusters and pools. Goal: prototype a light-weight smoothing + aggregation approach so product teams see stable per-pool utilization trends without losing short spike signals that might indicate real customer load.

Why this matters:
- Current dashboard (raw 5m samples) shows noisy oscillations for small pools (1-4 GPUs) which cause repeated alert churn.
- Ops needs an aggregated view for capacity planning: daily high-water mark, 95th percentile sustained windows, and an adjusted headroom metric that accounts for KV-cache warmups and short bursts.

Quick summary of observations from the export:
1) Small pools (pool_id starting with P-SM-) show median utilization 18-22% but a series of micro-spikes to 80-95% that last <6 minutes. Those spikes inflate 95th-percentile and trigger "low-headroom" flags.
2) Large pools (P-LG-) are smoother but show drift across regions: APAC clusters report ~6% higher baseline utilization than NA for the same workload mix.
3) Several clusters (cluster-kt4, cluster-sj2) had sustained elevated tail latency correlated with GPU-util >88% for >30m windows.

Data processing proposal (prototype steps):
- Inputs: daily csv export with these columns: timestamp, region, cluster_id, pool_id, gpu_count, util_pct (avg per-5m), token_rate, queued_requests.
- Pre-filter: remove maintenance windows flagged in metadata (meta_maintenance == true).
- Smoothing: two-stage smoothing for each pool_id:
  1) Short-term median filter: run a 3-sample median over the 5m samples (gives 15m window) to remove single-point spikes due to telemetry noise.
  2) Exponential smoothing with alpha tuned by pool size: alpha = min(0.3, 1/(1+sqrt(gpu_count))). Small pools get slightly heavier smoothing.
- Peak-preservation: keep a separate 'spike_score' track: raw_util - median(15m). If spike_score > 0.35*max_possible (i.e. >35 percentage pts) and lasts >= 2 samples mark as transient_burst.

Why this combo: median filter reduces telemetry blips; exponential smoothing produces a readable trend for capacity planning; the spike_score preserves actionable short bursts so alerts can be tuned to use both smoothed_util and transient_burst flags.

Sample CSV snippet (from export, anonymized):
timestamp,region,cluster_id,pool_id,gpu_count,util_pct,token_rate,queued_requests
2026-03-24T00:00Z,na,cluster-kt4,P-SM-17,2,14,830,0
2026-03-24T00:05Z,na,cluster-kt4,P-SM-17,2,16,920,0
2026-03-24T00:10Z,na,cluster-kt4,P-SM-17,2,92,3400,6    # short spike correlated with a bursty job
2026-03-24T00:15Z,na,cluster-kt4,P-SM-17,2,18,780,0
2026-03-24T00:20Z,na,cluster-kt4,P-SM-17,2,17,760,0

Derived columns we will publish in the sheet:
- util_smoothed_daily (float)  - final smoothed series aggregated to daily average
- util_95_adjusted (float) - 95th percentile computed on smoothed series but with transient bursts re-included for a separate alerting channel
- headroom_estimate (float) - (1 - util_95_adjusted) * capacity_multiplier; capacity_multiplier accounts for KV warming factor per model class (recommended default 0.9)
- transient_burst_count (int) - number of transient_burst windows per day per pool

Preliminary numbers (single-day rollup examples):
- P-SM-17 (na / cluster-kt4): gpu_count=2, raw_util_95=61%, util_smoothed_daily=21%, util_95_adjusted=49%, transient_burst_count=3 -> headroom_estimate=0.51*0.9=0.459 (46%)
- P-LG-04 (eu / cluster-am1): gpu_count=16, raw_util_95=34%, util_smoothed_daily=27%, util_95_adjusted=32%, transient_burst_count=0 -> headroom_estimate=0.68*0.9=0.612 (61%)

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Run smoothing pipeline on last 30 days of export and compare alerts count vs current raw thresholds. (Owner: Aisha) -> JIRA INFRA-1723 assigned.
- [ ] Add a per-pool 'burst_tolerance' knob in alerts so small pools are not noisy by default (Owner: Miguel).
- [ ] Create a short dashboard tile for "transient burst overlay" that toggles between raw and smoothed traces. (Owner: Renee)
- [ ] Validate KV-cache warming multiplier per model family with Research (defer, low priority).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is the 3-sample median too heavy for pools with 1 GPU? Might mask real short jobs that fully occupy that single GPU. Consider pool-size-aware median window (3 for >=2 GPUs, 1 for single-gpu pools).
- We should test smoothing on synthetic traces (Poisson job arrival + some 30s jobs) to measure false-negative rate for real bursts.
- How do we communicate revised headroom numbers to SRE and Customer Success? Need a one-pager and migration plan for alert thresholds.

Slack references and threads: #infra-capacity (thread: "noisy-small-pools"), #sre-oncall (for follow-up)

Rough timeline:
- Prototype smoothing on 30-day export: 2 days (script + CI run)
- Dashboard tile + PR for alerts: 3-4 days
- Team review and rollout: 1 week (staged canary to 10% of alerts)

Notes: this is a working doc — expect iterations. Keep raw CSVs in GCS under gs://redwood-infra-exports/pool-util/2026-03-*/ and link artifacts above.

If we have time in the sprint, evaluate whether a percentile-on-smoothed-series + spike-reinjection approach reduces alert noise by >=40% without missing legitimate capacity exhaustion events.

End of notes.
